handoffs.where: ledger 50 (1937 loss of Xinjiang, counterpart union-of-soviet-socialist-republics) and ledger 60 (1943-10 gain, same counterpart)
handoffs.what: Replace the loss/gain pair by a client tint (vassal_start 1937 / vassal_end 1943 with the USSR as suzerain) or drop it, so that no Xinjiang cell changes owner.
handoffs.why: Xinjiang stayed Chinese: Sheng Shicai's duty was 'to keep Xinjiang permanently a Chinese province' and the 1935 statement called annexation 'untrue'; the loss hands 5,499 cells to the USSR, whose dossier correctly does not draw them, so the compiler snaps them off in 1940 and Xinjiang is nobody's 1940-1943.

handoffs.what: Make republic-of-china (or nobody) the owner of the dissolved land and keep the Soviet role as the existing occupation events; the USSR should not be the successor owner of Manchuria, Hulunbuir, Ulanhot and Tongliao.
handoffs.why: The Soviet-Japanese War page gives 'Soviet occupation of Inner Mongolia and Manchuria until 1946', not annexation (only South Sakhalin and the Kurils were annexed); the dissolve gives about 5,400 cells to the USSR as owner in 1945 and its 1946 keyframe takes them away again (F045 snap).

handoffs.what: Check that the upper satrapies (Iran, Afghanistan, Central Asia and the Indus lands the Macedonian 315 shape reached) pass to Seleucus in 309; the macedonian-empire loss of 309 now names all of them and counterpart seleucid-empire.
handoffs.why: Babylonian War 311-309: Seleucus 'secured control over the eastern provinces'.
